source.authors: Mikhail N. Glukhovtsev, Addy Pross, Leo Radom
source.title: Gas-Phase Identity SN2 Reactions of Halide Anions with Methyl Halides: A High-Level Computational Study
source.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

barrier_evidence.method: G2(+) high-level ab initio molecular-orbital protocol applied across X = F, Cl, Br, I
barrier_evidence.mechanistic_path: conventional back-side Walden-inversion identity SN2 path through an ion-molecule complex and central saddle

overall_barrier.type: calculated 298 K overall activation enthalpy relative to separated reactants, DeltaH_dagger_overall

central_barrier.type: calculated 298 K central activation enthalpy from the ion-molecule complex to the central saddle
central_barrier.role: network-topology descriptor; not substituted for the separated-reactant overall barrier

barrier_evidence.source_comparison_note: The paper explicitly compares the calculated chloride barriers with prior experimental energetic estimates. The G2(+) protocol is nevertheless an ab initio method applied systematically across the halide series; no same-target rate fitting of the 9.8 kJ/mol value is disclosed. Agreement itself is not used here to select or promote the candidate.

source.authors: Stephan E. Barlow, Jane M. Van Doren, Veronica M. Bierbaum
source.title: The gas phase displacement reaction of chloride ion with methyl chloride as a function of kinetic energy
source.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

primary_rate_evidence_A.collision_energy_behavior: reported rate coefficient remains nearly constant up to approximately 0.4 eV center-of-mass collision energy; above approximately 0.5 eV a different high-energy exchange pathway becomes important
primary_rate_evidence_A.low_energy_mechanism: usual back-side SN2 attack at carbon

source.authors: Jane M. Van Doren, Charles H. DePuy, Veronica M. Bierbaum
source.title: Gas-phase isotope-exchange reactions with chloride ion

primary_rate_evidence_B.instrument: selected-ion flow tube at thermal energy
primary_rate_evidence_B.reported_result: the SN2 reaction of 37Cl- with methyl chloride is immeasurably slow at room temperature
primary_rate_evidence_B.source_interpretation: transition state is close to or projects above the energy of the separated reactants

comparator_conflict.reason: Two closely related primary studies from the same experimental group do not license a single zero-field thermal comparator without reconstructing the instrumental energy distributions. The 1988 SIFT-drift paper gives 3.5e-14 cm^3 s^-1 at 300 K, whereas the 1989 thermal selected-ion-flow-tube study calls the same isotope-exchange reaction immeasurably slow at room temperature.
forbidden_resolution: choose the 1988 value because it agrees better with a computed barrier
treat gas temperature as proof that the drift-field ion kinetic-energy distribution is thermal
replace the missing thermal comparator with the guided-ion-beam translational threshold

source.authors: Susan C. Tucker, Donald G. Truhlar
source.title: A six-body potential energy surface for the SN2 reaction Cl-(g) + CH3Cl(g) and a variational transition-state-theory calculation of the rate constant
source.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

same_target_model_quarantine.result: The reported semiempirical gas-phase barrier of 3.1 kcal/mol was chosen to reproduce the experimental 300 K rate coefficient.

representation_note: The physical path contains a reactant ion-molecule complex and central saddle; nonstatistical scattering and recrossing literature prevents reducing the observed exchange kinetics to an unqualified one-saddle rate picture.
next_gate: Reconstruct the 1988 SIFT-drift ion kinetic-energy distribution, field strength and effective collision-energy regime and the 1989 thermal SIFT detection limit. A qualifying comparator requires a numerical experimentally observed rate coefficient under a regime that can be explicitly mapped to the 298 K gas-phase barrier representation. If the 1988 value is demonstrably a non-zero-field drift coefficient, retain it as a separate energetic-regime observable rather than a thermal Atlas comparator.
